clue.text: Pottery keeping recently-made article in reserve

indicators.note: a store keeping something holds it within, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: a reserve is a store, a stock put by
something recently made is new
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pottery shop holds back a freshly made piece as a spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard-fired type of ceramic, so it is a kind of pottery.

clue.text: This ensures one doesn't get 9 across!

definitions.text: This ensures one doesn't get 9 across!

parts.words: This ensures one doesn't get 9 across!
parts.note: 9 across means angered, but read literally it means pricked by a sewing needle; the finger guard worn when sewing stops that happening

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a person from getting angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 9 across is NEEDLED; taken literally, being needled is being jabbed by a needle, which a sewer's metal finger cap prevents.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble protects the fingertip from the needle's point while sewing.

clue.text: So-called lion-man running wild

indicators.note: something running wild is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supposed half-lion, half-man creature is loose and rampaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists in name only, just as a so-called thing is merely called that.

clue.text: A know-all will be sensible over port

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes before it

parts.note: a sensible person is wise
Acre is a port city in Israel

explanation.surface: Someone who knows everything will behave sensibly about fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who pretends to know everything, a smart alec.

clue.text: In general a guy retires to paint

indicators.note: something that retires goes back, so the assembled letters are read backwards in this down entry
a guy in a general places the guy's word inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: Among the generals, one fellow goes into retirement to take up painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee is the Confederate general of the American Civil War. In a down clue, 'retires' (goes back) reads the result upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamel is to coat a surface with a glossy finish, a form of painting.

clue.text: Tread and wade about in stagnant pond perhaps

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Walking and wading through a still, murky pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead water is still water with no current, of which a stagnant pond is an example.

clue.text: Heartless rogue taken in by a woman before now

indicators.note: something taken in by another sits inside it

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: with its heart gone, only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A villain with no heart is fooled by a woman, as has happened before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' leaves R and E from 'rogue'; 'taken in by' sets them inside A LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time, earlier than now.

clue.text: Leader given aid to rile rebels

indicators.note: rebels rise against order, so these letters break ranks and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leader gets help in stirring up rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' is not a person here: a leader is a newspaper's opinion column.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the main opinion article, also called an editorial.

clue.text: Angered by want-showed some initiative

parts.note: want means need
to take the initiative is to lead, so showed some initiative is led

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed by poverty but took the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be irritated or provoked, so angered.

clue.text: The underworld girl's release

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and its name
a miss is a girl; the 's means is and joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A young woman from hell gets set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss is to send away or let go, so to release.

clue.text: Most abandoned divine quarters in dull surroundings

indicators.note: a word in surroundings is enclosed, so the dull word wraps the others

parts.note: mat (or matt) means dull, without shine
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine
E and S, east and south, are compass quarters

explanation.surface: A clergyman's lodgings set in drab surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean wild and uninhibited, so most abandoned means most wildly crazy.

clue.text: Taking a trip carrying cake in plenty

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside

parts.note: to trip the light fantastic is to dance, so a trip is a dance
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: Going on a journey with lots of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a great quantity, more than enough.

clue.text: A miner's dog right?

parts.note: a collie is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Is the dog belonging to a mine worker correct?
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner.

clue.text: A shrub no dealer can possibly supply

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: This bush cannot be supplied by any seller.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a poisonous evergreen flowering bush.

clue.text: Seller of fruit-about five hundred pounds

indicators.note: the fruit's word goes about the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
L (libra) is the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: A fruit vendor charging around five hundred pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling vendor of small goods.

clue.text: An American always on the level

definitions.text: An American always on the level

parts.words: An American always on the level
parts.note: seems to describe an honest American, but means a settler living on the flat grasslands of the Great Plains

explanation.surface: An American who is always honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsmen were inhabitants of the North American Great Plains, flat country.

clue.text: Archer's tip

parts.note: could be a piece of advice from a bowman, but is the pointed end of what such a person shoots

explanation.surface: Advice from an archer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrowhead is the pointed tip of an arrow, the archer's missile.

clue.text: Substitute for two quite different materials

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
lace is an openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Swapping one fabric for a completely different one.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to put another thing in its place, to substitute.

clue.text: An entertainer from Macedonia endlessly on the move

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifted around into a new order
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A performer travelling out of Macedonia without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts 'Macedonia' to MACEDONI; 'on the move' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a performer who entertains by making people laugh.

clue.text: Dance around easy street in wild delight!

indicators.note: letters made to dance are jumbled into another order

parts.note: C (circa) means around

explanation.surface: Someone dances around an easy street, thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; 'around' gives C, for circa, the Latin abbreviation used with approximate dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is overwhelming joy or rapture.

clue.text: Trial resulting from gold transaction

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a deal is a transaction

explanation.surface: A hard experience came from trading in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or testing experience, a trial.

clue.text: An excavator causing a certain irritation in the German

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: der is a German word for the
an itch is a particular irritation

explanation.surface: A digger brings an irritation to a German man.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditcher is someone or something that digs trenches.

clue.text: The course is not commonly about the Orient

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of is not
re means about or concerning
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: The route is not, in common speech, about the East.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse where the Grand National steeplechase is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous British racecourse for horse racing.

clue.text: Given short measure, none scoffed, being immature

parts.note: an inch is a short unit of length
O is zero, none
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A child given a tiny portion eats nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only just begun, not yet fully formed or developed.

clue.text: Special gift-a story on the National Trust

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A present: a book about the National Trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural ability or aptitude, a gift.

clue.text: Entering a strange country

indicators.note: strange indicates the letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Going into a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' reads as a verb but is anagram fodder; 'strange' scrambles it. 'The Argentine' is an old name for Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine is an old name for Argentina, a South American country.

clue.text: Bag some bargains at Chelsea jumble-sales

indicators.note: some of the words supply letters, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Picking up good buys at jumble sales in Chelsea, a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, often for school books.

clue.text: He's clear about fish

definitions.note: names a man, the answer being a man's first name

indicators.note: the clear word goes about the fish word, enclosing it

parts.note: to rid is to clear
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: A man is free of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard is a common male given name, so a he.

clue.text: Don't make a scholar turn colour!

indicators.note: turn means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar
to stain is to colour

explanation.surface: An instruction not to dye a student another colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from doing something, so the imperative means refrain.
